acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner-wife seeks transfer of divorce petition filed by respondent-husband under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Petitioner-wife claims hardship in traveling from Jhajjar to Narnaul for court proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble the Apex Court has held as under: '9. The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.'
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, AIR 2022 SC 4318

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both parties, their social strata, behavioural pattern, standard of life prior to and subsequent to marriage.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble the Apex Court has held as under: '9. The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.'
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, AIR 2022 SC 4318

legal_principles.principle: When two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble the Apex Court has held as under: '10. Further, when two or more proceedings are pending in different Courts between the same parties which raise common question of fact and law, and when the decisions in the cases are interdependent, it is desirable that they should be tried together by the same Judge so as to avoid multiplicity in trial of the same issues and conflict of decisions.'
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya v. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, AIR 2022 SC 4318
keywords: common question of fact and law

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants.
legal_principles.held: Hon'ble the Apex Court has observed that 'while deciding the transfer application, the Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one court to another should ordinary be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.'
cited_cases: Rajani Kishor Pradeshi v. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) 12 SCC 237

outcome.final_order: Transfer of petition allowed to any Court of competent jurisdiction at Narnaul.
